newsitem.title: MEXICO: Envoy sees good U.S.-Mexican dialogue continuing.
newsitem.headline: Envoy sees good U.S.-Mexican dialogue continuing.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's election victory ensures a continued "positive dialogue" between the United States and Mexico, Mexico's ambassador to the United States said on Wednesday.

But Mexico faces a big challenge from the Republican-controlled Congress, Jesus Silva Herzog said in a live television interview from Washington, the first official Mexican reaction to the election results.
"Bill Clinton has been a friendly president toward Mexico and this (victory) ensures a constructive and positive dialogue for the next four years," Silva said.
But he said a "fundamental part" of the U.S.-Mexican agenda would take many years to resolve.
"The border cannot be rubbed out, immigration is not going to disappear, nor drug trafficking. Trade problems can be smoothed over, but others will appear," he added.

On the continued Republican control of Congress, Silva said Mexico had a "magnificent relationship" with U.S. government agencies. But he added: "I cannot say the same for Congress, it is one of the big challenges we face."

Clinton used presidential powers to bail out Mexico with a $20 billion rescue package in the 1995 economic crisis after a bungled peso devaluation took the country to the brink of collapse. Congress had planned to block financial aid.
President Ernesto Zedillo was expected to congratulate Clinton later in the day.
